 Above & Beyond to Debut Anjunabeats Classics Set at Dreamstate
 By Bryson Page - November 20, 2026 
 Above & Beyond are set to perform a first-ever Anjunabeats Classics set at Dreamstate Southern California this Saturday, November 21. The GRAMMY-nominated trio — Jono Grant, Paavo Siljamäki and Tony McGuinness — will use the performance to dig back through more than 25 years of Anjunabeats history, revisiting the records that built the label into one of trance music’s most recognizable names.
 Since founding Anjunabeats in 2000, Above & Beyond have steadily grown the label from a scrappy independent imprint into a global operation with a catalog spanning well over two decades of trance, progressive and electronic music. The trio’s own sound has shifted plenty over the years, but the early records that put Anjunabeats on the map remain central to how fans identify the group.
 This marks the first time the trio has built an entire set strictly around that back catalog. Instead of leaning on new or unreleased material, as is typical for most of their shows, the Classics set will focus squarely on the tracks that defined Anjunabeats’ formative years. It’s a chance for longtime Anjunafamily members to reconnect with the music that hooked them in the first place, and for newer fans to get a crash course in a pretty important chapter of the label’s story.
 Dreamstate feels like the right venue for it. The festival has built its identity around trance in all its forms, pulling together artists and fans spanning multiple generations of the genre. A dedicated Classics set from Above & Beyond fits neatly into that framework — a tribute to the sound that helped shape modern trance, performed for the community that’s kept it alive.
 The announcement lands during a particularly busy stretch for the group. Following the release of their fifth studio album, Bigger Than All Of Us , Above & Beyond ran an extensive international tour that included a North American amphitheater run along with dates across Europe and Australia. In September, they brought the show back to Washington State’s Gorge Amphitheatre for ABGT700 , their milestone Group Therapy celebration that drew close to 20,000 fans across three days of Anjunabeats and Anjunadeep programming.
 More recently, the trio wrapped their four-city Anjunabeats Warehouse Tour through Glasgow, Liverpool, Birmingham and Bristol, bringing along a mix of established label names and newer talent. That tour heads to Asia next, with stops planned in Kuala Lumpur and Singapore — another sign of just how far the Anjunabeats community has spread since those early 2000s releases.
 Most of what Above & Beyond have been doing lately points forward — new albums, new tours, new artists on the label roster. The Dreamstate set flips that script, at least for one night, giving fans a dedicated look back at the records and moments that built Anjunabeats into what it is today.
 Above & Beyond’s Anjunabeats Classics set takes place this Saturday, November 21, at Dreamstate SoCal.
